bull_bear.body:
- Deep in-house manufacturing engineering: the Company builds and rebuilds its own machines end-to-end from design to finishing, having built/rebuilt 1,162 machines to date, converted 16 two-wheeler Rod CNC machines from manual to automatic mode and manufactured 27 SPM machines in-house, using scrap iron and steel from old machines as raw material.
- Long-running Total Productive Maintenance programme run with JIPM (Japan) and CII TPM Club India, with TPM Excellence 'Category A' awards for the Gurugram (2008) and Manesar (2010) plants and JIPM TPM Excellence Consistency Awards for both plants in 2013.
- Lean manufacturing clubbed with TPM (Value Stream Mapping workshop conducted through JMAC Japan), producing '10S' machines that consume less electricity, space, consumables, manpower, set-up and cycle time, lowering cost of manufacturing.
- Strategic technology collaborations with Astemo (Japan), Soben (France) and TFX Suspension (Netherlands) that expand access to advanced premium suspension technologies for a segment historically served through imports.
- Digital backbone upgraded during the year through a successful transition from SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA, described as strengthening process integration, operational visibility and data-driven decision-making and providing a scalable foundation for future growth.
- Green Vendor Development Programme run since 2009-10 to conserve water and energy, minimise waste, replace hazardous chemicals and achieve 100 percent legal compliance across the supply base.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Electrification of the vehicle parc erodes demand for conventional ICE-related components — MD&A Risks and Concerns calls the accelerated transition to electric mobility one of the key challenges: increasing EV adoption 'is expected to gradually alter demand patterns for conventional internal combustion engine (ICE)-related components, particularly engine and transmission systems, thereby requiring substantial investments in technology upgradation, product diversification, localisation, and research & development.' The Outlook also warns of consolidation and rationalisation across selected conventional product segments.
- Single-product, narrow end-market concentration — All products of the Company fall in one primary business segment - Shock Absorber (front forks, rear cushions, struts, gas springs/rear door lifters) - so there is no segmental diversification to absorb a demand shock. The Board's own identified risk list includes 'Over dependence on limited user segment base'.
- Dependence on technology collaborators — 'Dependence on Collaborators' is one of the risks the Board has explicitly identified. Product and technology access runs through Astemo (Japan) - also an enterprise with significant influence over the Company and the counterparty for royalty, design-and-drawing fees and intangible-asset purchases - while the newer Soben (France) and TFX Suspension (Netherlands) collaborations are 'still at an early stage and have yet to translate into commercial supplies'.
- Input-cost volatility and raw-material price increases — The MD&A flags volatility in raw material prices, inflationary pressures and rising energy and transportation costs; the Board's risk list includes 'Increase in raw material/component prices'. The Chairman states that input-cost volatility, together with the fixed cost of technology and digital-infrastructure investment, 'affected profitability in the short term' in FY 2025-26.
- Intensifying competition and margin compression — 'Intensifying Competition' and 'Declining margins' are both named in the Board's identified risk list - a structural pressure for a single-product tier-1 supplier selling to a concentrated OEM customer base.
- Supply-chain disruption, semiconductor availability and currency exposure — MD&A cites supply chain disruptions, semiconductor availability, logistics constraints and fluctuations in foreign exchange rates; mitigation is described only as vendor diversification, supply chain monitoring, cost optimisation and liquidity management.
- Rising regulatory and compliance cost from emission, safety and environmental norms — MD&A states that stricter emission norms, Bharat NCAP safety regulations and evolving environmental compliance requirements 'may lead to higher capital expenditure and operational costs' for manufacturers and component suppliers. The Board's risk list separately names 'Imposition of strict environmental / safety / regulatory regulations'.
- Listing-compliance and insider-trading control lapses observed during the year — The Directors' Report discloses that Board strength fell below the six-director minimum under Regulation 17(1)(c) from April 08, 2025 to May 26, 2025 (about 48 days) after Mr. Kazuhiro Nishioka's cessation; a Regulation 30 outcome-of-board-meeting submission to NSE was delayed by about 3 hours 58 minutes; and the Secretarial Auditors observed that certain instances of UPSI sharing were not fully captured in the Structured Digital Database, alongside an observation on timely circulation of draft Minutes.
- Product liability and disaster exposure — 'Product liability' and 'Risk of natural or manmade disasters' are named in the Board's identified risk list, alongside 'Economic downturn' - relevant for a safety-critical suspension component supplied to OEMs from three concentrated manufacturing sites at Gurugram, Manesar and Haridwar.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Munjal Showa Limited manufactures shock absorbers for the Indian automotive industry; the annual report states that all products of the Company come under a single primary business segment, i.e. Shock Absorber, whose variants are Front Forks, Rear Cushions, Struts and Gas Spring/Rear Door Lifters. The Company supplies Indian OEMs and has strengthened its presence in the premium motorcycle segment while building engineering capability for emerging mobility applications including electric vehicles. Manufacturing is run on lean manufacturing, Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) and extensive in-house low-cost automation, with machines designed and built in-house.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the Company's position in the premium motorcycle segment and move progressively towards higher-value engineering solutions, including Inverted Front Fork Technology shock absorbers for prime-segment motorcycles.
- Deepen engineering capability through strategic technology collaborations with Astemo (Japan), Soben (France) and TFX Suspension (Netherlands) to access advanced premium suspension technologies for a segment historically served through imports.
- Focus R&D on indigenous engineering and product development capability for emerging mobility applications, including electric vehicles.
- Sustain manufacturing excellence through lean manufacturing, Total Productive Maintenance and in-house low-cost automation - designing and building its own machines end-to-end, including Industry 4.0-configured SPM machines (27 for Floating Piston Technology in Rear Cushions, launched with the ADLA Hero model, and 24 for Front Inverted Technology).
- Continue digitalisation after the transition from SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA, described as a scalable foundation for future growth through better process integration, operational visibility and data-driven decision-making.
- Sustainability through investment in energy-efficient manufacturing, responsible resource use and progressively stronger ESG disclosure and transparency; a Green Vendor Development Programme has run since 2009-10.
- Build talent and technical skills, including through the Government's NEEM and NAPS schemes, employee engagement programmes and leadership/functional capability development to meet future talent requirements.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The annual report describes no greenfield plant or capacity-addition project. Manufacturing remains at the three existing facilities at Gurugram, Haridwar and Manesar, and 'expansion' is expressed as capability build-out rather than tonnage: in-house manufacture of 27 SPM machines for Floating Piston Technology in the Rear Cushion segment, successfully launched with the ADLA Hero model, and 24 SPM machines for Front Inverted Technology, with all machines under both technologies conforming to Industry 4.0 configuration, supporting Inverted Front Fork Technology shock absorbers for prime-segment motorcycles. A fully automatic valve counting and dispensing machine was developed in-house, and a second auto valve counting machine for the Honda and Maruti segment is stated to be launched by end June 2026. A further seven major projects are described as in the pipeline. The Company has built and rebuilt 1,162 machines to date and converted 16 two-wheeler Rod CNC machines from manual to automatic mode, with automation also achieved in most damper-case and bottom-tube welding processes across all three plants. Other capability investments during the year were the transition from SAP ECC to SAP S/4HANA and continued technology collaborations with Astemo (Japan), Soben (France) and TFX Suspension (Netherlands), the latter two still pre-commercial.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand recovered meaningfully after the GST rate rationalisation announced in September 2025 following a relatively subdued first half, producing a strong festive season and a record year for the Indian auto component industry, which surpassed Rs 7.6 lakh crore in turnover.
- Consumer preferences continue to evolve towards premium vehicle segments while electric mobility gains momentum, particularly in two-wheelers - structural shifts management says create new opportunities for suppliers with strong engineering capabilities and manufacturing discipline.
- Record domestic vehicle demand in FY 2025-26: Indian vehicle production rose to 3,47,08,984 units from 3,10,34,174 units, with SIAM domestic sales at record levels across passenger vehicles (46.43 lakh), commercial vehicles (10.80 lakh), three-wheelers (8.36 lakh) and two-wheelers (217.06 lakh).
- Increasing localisation and government policy support - PLI for Automobile and Auto Components, PM E-DRIVE, Make in India, Bharat NCAP, vehicle scrappage policy - expected to strengthen the domestic manufacturing ecosystem and component demand.
- Export-led momentum under the China+1 sourcing strategy: ACMA-McKinsey projects India's auto component exports at US$ 70-100 billion by FY 2030 and industry size of US$ 200 billion by 2030; FY25 exports rose 8% to US$ 22.9 billion with a US$ 453 million trade surplus.
- Structural transformation towards electrification, digitalisation and connected mobility is expected to reduce dependence on conventional ICE-related components (particularly engine and transmission systems) over the medium to long term, requiring investment in EV-compatible products, technology upgradation and product diversification.
- Input-cost volatility, fixed cost of technology and the investments made to strengthen digital infrastructure affected profitability in the short term, per the Chairman's letter.
